narrative.summary: Paraguay has no AI law or adopted national AI strategy. The Supreme Court's 2026 operational policy sets binding guidelines for the use of AI systems, including generative AI, in the Judiciary. Law No. 7593/2025 on personal data protection, published in November 2025 and due to enter into force 24 months later, gives people the right to have automated decisions reviewed and contested, requires impact assessments for automated profiling with significant effects, and creates a data protection agency within the ICT ministry (MITIC). MITIC is preparing a national AI roadmap after a UNESCO readiness assessment, and AI bills are pending in Congress.
lead_institutions: Ministerio de Tecnologías de la Información y Comunicación (MITIC)
narrative.review_notes: Reviewed again on 18 October 2026: the Congress library, the Chamber of Deputies, the central bank and the telecoms regulator were checked, and the 2025 data protection law was added. Not yet verified from the official text: the AI bills and the national AI roadmap, which remain pending as leads, and material from the Official Gazette, the Presidency, MITIC, the Senate, the bill system and the procurement agency.

instruments.official_title: Política Operacional que establece directrices para el uso de sistemas de inteligencia artificial en el Poder Judicial
instruments.english_title: Operational Policy establishing guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence systems in the Judiciary (approved by Supreme Court Resolution No. 12,677)
instruments.issuing_authority: Supreme Court of Justice (Corte Suprema de Justicia)
instruments.current_status: Approved by Supreme Court Resolution No. 12.677 of 4 March 2026 (Version 1), which authorises its application; the Poder Judicial announced it on 9 April 2026. A working group set up under Acta No. 5/2025 of the Consejo de Superintendencia reports periodically to the Internal Control Committee on implementation.
instruments.summary: Supreme Court resolution approving a binding operational policy for magistrates and officials of the Paraguayan Judiciary who use, develop, acquire or supervise AI systems, covering existing and future, in-house and third-party systems. It sets principles of human oversight, transparency and open justice, among others, lists permitted support uses (legal research, summaries, translation, draft structuring) subject to human verification, and prohibits delegating judicial or administrative decisions to AI, fully automating processes affecting fundamental rights, determining guilt or setting penalties without human intervention. It defines generative AI, LLMs, chatbots and agents, and addresses hallucinations, over-reliance and algorithmic bias.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding AI-use rules issued by a Paraguayan state body; governs AI use across the entire judiciary.

instruments.official_title: Ley N° 7593/2025 De Protección de Datos Personales en la República del Paraguay
instruments.english_title: Law No. 7593/2025 on Personal Data Protection in the Republic of Paraguay
instruments.current_status: Passed by the Chamber of Deputies on 14 October 2025 and the Senate on 5 November 2025; promulgated and published on 27 November 2025 according to the Congress library's official law collection. Article 57 provides that it enters into force 24 months after its official publication, and the Executive must issue implementing regulations within 24 months of publication in the Official Gazette. The text read is the Congress library's official copy.
instruments.summary: Comprehensive personal data protection law applying to wholly or partly automated processing by public and private controllers and processors in Paraguay or targeting people in Paraguay. It defines profiling, requires a data protection impact assessment for systematic automated evaluation (including profiling) that produces legal or similarly significant effects, and requires controllers to disclose automated decisions and meaningful information about the logic involved. Article 33 gives data subjects the right to request review of automated or semi-automated decisions that affect them, to express their view and to contest the decision, and creates the National Personal Data Protection Agency within MITIC as supervisory authority.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sets binding rules on automated decision-making, profiling and impact assessments that govern AI systems processing personal data, and creates the authority that will supervise them.
